A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Markov logic network approach is a powerful framework for solving the problem of optical chemical structure recognition.

we are able to recognize the chemical structure from an image with an accuracy of 97.3% (on a data set of 1000 images) and with an accuracy of more than 90% even when the image is degraded by a low-pass filtering.

we have developed an innovative method for optical chemical structure recognition that is able to cope with low-resolution images and to provide a structured output representation of the recognized molecule, with a performance comparable to the current state-of-art methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of pattern recognition with knowledge representation and reasoning can be successfully applied to the challenging problem of optical structure recognition, yielding a system which is robust to the presence of noise and artifacts, and able to handle low-resolution and degraded images.

probabilistic graphical models can be used as the unifying framework for the integration of low-level and high-level processing, and can provide a principled way for incorporating domain knowledge in the form of probabilistic rules.
